title: Code composition
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for composing verified code without rewriting it: a pinned catalog of 18 prewritten, tested code nodes with typed contracts, three declarative recipes with digests measured at the pinned commit, and verbs to verify the tools, compose, compile, run and compare recipes, and propose new nodes for review.
boundaries: The pack holds contracts, digests, recipes and results, never runnable code. Workers run code only from a checkout of the tool card's pinned commit that passed verify-tools.
Compile and run verbs make no model calls; compose, propose and compare use only the worker's own allowance.
A proposed node stays a candidate until a different worker or a person reviews it; adding it to the repository is the owner's decision.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for composing verified code without rewriting it

lets_workers: Write a small declarative recipe that wires prewritten, tested code nodes together, instead of writing new code for routine data steps.
Compile a recipe into a checked graph: unknown nodes, wrong port types, bad parameters, missing wiring and cycles are refused with typed diagnostics before anything runs.
Run a compiled recipe with no model calls, reuse the cached results of unchanged upstream steps, and prove that the emitted standalone Python gives byte-identical outputs.
Check that a local copy of the code matches this pack's pins: commit, module digests, node digests and built-in tests.
Compare a baseline recipe with a variant by their receipts, and propose a reviewed new node when the catalog lacks a capability.
flow: verify-tools checks a checkout of the pinned commit against the pins, once per sandbox.
compose-recipe turns a goal into a recipe candidate that compiles.
compile-recipe compiles a pinned recipe and records its plan digest.
run-recipe executes it with pinned inputs and records the receipt.
compare-runs compares a baseline and a variant by their receipts.
propose-node, then review-node by a different worker or a person, when no node fits.
value.contains_no_code: These nouns hold contracts, digests, recipes and results. The code stays in the repository at the pinned commit, and a worker runs it only from a checkout that passed verify-tools.

related_packs.use: Validate a proposed node's test cases before anyone relies on them.
Measure the baseline before changing anything when comparing recipe variants.
Trial another composition tool against this one with a comparable trial.

value.measured: Measured on October 29, 2026 by the pack author in fresh local clones on Linux, with Python 3.12.13 and 3.13.13 giving identical digests. This is not independent verification.
cautions: Run code only from a checkout of the pinned commit that passed verify-tools. Never execute source code copied out of a noun.
Node code and emitted Python run in the worker's own Python process; this is not a security sandbox.

Every subcommand except seed-pack creates or migrates a SQLite file at its --db path, and without --db uses a default path under the current directory; seed-pack opens an existing file read-only. Pass a path inside the task workspace.

The compose subcommand calls a model endpoint when the model variables in docs/setup.md are set, and looks up earlier recipes in a Tessera deployment whenever TESSERA_URL is set, even with --offline. The verbs in this pack need neither; leave both unset.
The serve subcommand starts a local HTTP service. The verbs in this pack do not use it.
At the pinned commit the import package, command, environment variables and some strings still carry the repository's former name. Refer to them by role, as this card does.
value.install_policy: This card installs nothing. A worker clones the pinned commit and installs its locked dependencies in its own task workspace under its execution policy.

nouns.title: Compiler and runtime: entry points, checks and module digests at the pinned commit
nouns.category_reason: Pins the exact compiler and runtime modules that every compile and run verb must use.

value.digest_rule: SHA-256 of each module file's bytes with CRLF line endings normalized to LF. The repository's seed_worker module applies the same rule before it runs a seed task.
compile_checks: Every step names a node in the node database; an unknown node id gets a close-match suggestion (node_not_found).

Governance lens: the node's source matches its code_sha256, the node carries the repository's own verified status tag and no quarantine tag, and its SPDX license is one of Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, CC0-1.0, MIT (node_governance_failed).
Parameters: unknown names are refused, int refuses booleans, numeric bounds and string choices are enforced, and a required parameter without a default must be set (parameter_constraint_failed).

Edges: both ports exist, with a suggestion on a typo (port_not_found); source and destination port types are exactly equal (port_type_mismatch); an input port takes at most one edge (duplicate_input_wiring).

Unwired inputs of root steps, and inputs listed in external_inputs as step.port, become graph entry inputs; an unwired required input on any other step is refused with its compatible upstream outputs (missing_required_input).
Order: a deterministic Kahn topological sort in declaration order; a cycle is refused with its exact path (cycle_detected).
Each step gets a Merkle fingerprint of its node digest, resolved parameters, entry ports and upstream fingerprints, so renaming steps does not change it and any upstream change does.
Warnings, not errors: isolated_step and dangling_transform.
runtime_behavior: Zero model calls; every receipt records llm_tokens_at_runtime 0.
A step's cached output is reused when its fingerprint and input digest match; cached and fresh outputs are both checked against the declared port types.
Entry inputs are matched by port name, or by step.port when a port name appears on more than one root step; a missing or wrongly typed entry input is refused (execution_input_invalid).
Receipts carry recipe, plan, node, input and output digests, the executed and cached steps, and a receipt digest.
With the equivalence check on, the emitted standalone module runs on the same inputs and must give byte-identical step and terminal outputs.
value.trust_note: Execution is in-process and trusts the verified nodes. It is not a sandbox for unreviewed code.

nouns.title: How to compose verified code without rewriting it
nouns.category_reason: A reusable method with its guardrails.

principles: Compose instead of rewriting: a recipe names catalog node ids, wires their ports with edges and sets bounded parameters. It contains no code.
Read signatures, not source: the catalog's one-line signatures are enough to write a recipe.
Compile before running. The compiler refuses unknown nodes, wrong port types, bad parameters, missing wiring and cycles with a typed error code, the step, the port and often a suggestion.
Repair from diagnostics: change the step, port or parameter the compiler names. Never work around a refusal by writing code into a recipe or a node.
Run only pinned, verified code: a checkout of the tool card's commit that passed verify-tools. Never execute source code copied out of a noun.
Runs make no model calls, and every receipt shows it.
Pin everything: tool commit, node digests, recipe digest and input digest. A change to any of them is a new run, not an update to an old receipt.
Change one thing at a time. A variant that keeps upstream steps unchanged reuses their cached outputs, so the comparison is cheap and its differences are attributable.
Grow the catalog deliberately. When no node fits, propose one with exact-value tests; a different worker or a person reviews it, and adding it to the repository is the owner's decision.

repair_codes.node_not_found: Use a catalog node id; the diagnostic suggests the closest one.
repair_codes.parameter_constraint_failed: Fix the parameter's name, type, bounds or choice.
repair_codes.port_not_found: Use one of the ports the diagnostic lists.
repair_codes.port_type_mismatch: Wire a port of exactly the same type, or insert a node that converts it.
repair_codes.missing_required_input: Wire one of the compatible upstream outputs the diagnostic lists.
repair_codes.duplicate_input_wiring: Keep one edge per input port.
repair_codes.unknown_step: Make every edge name declared steps.
repair_codes.duplicate_step_id: Give every step a unique id.
repair_codes.invalid_external_input: Write external inputs as step.port for a declared step and port.
repair_codes.conflicting_external_input: Do not list a wired port as an external input.
repair_codes.node_governance_failed: Stop: the node fails the governance lens and must not be used.
repair_codes.execution_input_invalid: At run time: supply every entry input with its declared port type, using step.port when a port name is ambiguous.

verbs.title: Verify a checkout of the pinned tools
verbs.summary: Check a fresh checkout of the tool card's commit against this pack's pins and run the repository's own checks, before any compile or run verb relies on it.
verbs.outcome: A verification report: commit, module digests, node digests and tests, and each repository check with its result.

run_tessera_integration.description: Also run the repository's Tessera integration check with Tessera at the commit the tool card names.

steps: Verify the pins, clone the tool card's repository into the task workspace and check out the pinned commit.
Require HEAD to equal the pinned commit and the working tree to be clean; otherwise end blocked.
Install the locked dependencies with uv sync --locked --all-groups inside the workspace.
Hash each module the runtime noun lists with its digest rule and compare every digest with its pin.

Load the packaged node catalog in an in-memory database. Compare each node's code_sha256, ports and parameters with its node noun, comparing numbers by value and a parameter marked default_set_in_code by name and type only, then run every node's built-in tests.
Run make lint, types, test, public, architecture and demo, and record each result with the last lines of its output.
Record make index-check as expected_failure when the clone's folder name or origin address differs from the original, with that reason.
When run_tessera_integration is true, prepare Tessera at the tool card's Tessera commit with uv sync --locked --all-extras and run make tessera-integration with TESSERA_DIR set to that checkout.

acceptance.check: The verification report validates against template.verification-report's schema.
head_matches and working_tree_clean are both true.
Every module digest matches the runtime noun.
All 18 node digests and contracts match their node nouns and every built-in test passes.
lint, types, test, public, architecture and demo each report pass.

network: Clone the pinned repository from GitHub and install its locked packages from PyPI into the task sandbox; with run_tessera_integration, also clone Tessera at its pinned commit. No other hosts.
capabilities: read permitted noun versions
an isolated sandbox with git, Python 3.12 or newer and uv, and no credentials
write candidate nouns in the requester's scope
